Subject: Re: Annual prepay schedule — initial ask

Michael —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we formalize internal planning, finance asked me to get clarity on a specific structure that would work for us: we want an annual prepay but with the ability to frontload a modest additional credit (what our CFO called a "springboard" credit) to cover aggressive early-quarter growth. Key constraints:

- The springboard can't create an open-ended clawback risk — finance wants a cap on repayment if usage underperforms.
- Any repayment/true-up should be quarterly with a clear waterfall (first draw against monthly usage, then quarterly true-up, then capped clawback).
- We want the option for limited carryover into Q2 if we over-commit in Q1 but stay within 120% of forecast.

Can Redwood outline an example wallet drawdown and a repayment waterfall you would accept commercially? Also need to understand what discount tiers you're willing to offer for a 2-year commitment vs. annual renewals.

Attaching our internal forecast for context. Happy to hop on a quick call — prefer Thurs morning PT.

Best,

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>

Claire —

Thanks for the clear constraints. Below is a pragmatic construct that balances your need for early runway with Redwood's desire to keep exposure limited. I kept terms simple so your legal/finance teams can model quickly.

High-level proposal (annual prepay with springboard):

1) Base annual prepay wallet: customer prepays $X for the year; wallet draws against usage monthly.

2) Springboard credit: an upfront additional credit equal to up to 25% of Q1 forecast (configurable, default 15%). This is paid as a discounted advance (we apply a one-time 20% uplift on token-equivalent credit to fund early growth).

3) Repayment waterfall (applies only if cumulative usage < committed drawdown at 90/180/270 days):
   - Step A: Monthly usage reduces wallet first (no clawback while monthly usage >= 75% of monthly forecast).
   - Step B: Quarterly true-up (30 days after quarter close) — shortfall deducted from the springboard up to a cap.
   - Step C: Residual clawback: capped at 40% of the original springboard amount (we can consider 25% cap on multi-year deals).

4) Carryover: unused credits beyond the springboard can carry into Q2 up to 20% of quarterly forecast; anything beyond is forfeited or applied to Q2 at a lower conversion (e.g., 0.5x).

5) Discounts:
   - 1yr commit: standard tiered volume discounts (see attached commercial_summary_v2.pdf).
   - 2yr commit: additional 7–10% on committed spend and ability to increase springboard cap by 10 percentage points.

This structure aims to (a) give you runway for early growth, (b) limit Redwood's downside via a capped clawback and quarterly true-ups, and (c) provide upside on longer commitments.

I attached: Draft_SOW_and_payment_schedule.xlsx (example payment cadence) and a simple diagram (wallet_drawdown_example.png).

If this reads well, Marissa will run numbers and propose a compact commercial term-sheet. We're available Thurs 9:30am PT for a quick align.

Best,

Claire —

Looping in Karthik and our contracts alias so we can move to a short-form term-sheet if you're aligned on principles. A couple of practical tweaks to Michael's construct we typically apply:

- Frontload discount: we can apply a 5% additional discount on the first 3 months of usage (applied as an extra credit) if you take a 2-year commitment and a minimum annual/yr-1 prepay threshold.
- Springboard repayment sequence: true-up quarterly, but we propose a 90-day grace window before any clawback on the springboard to give you operational time to ramp.
- Clawback cap: for 1yr deals we typically cap at 40%; for 2yr deals we can set at 25% as Michael noted.
- Replenishment: if monthly usage exceeds forecast, the wallet auto-replenishes from committed credit; if it underperforms, we reconcile at quarter close.

Next step: if you confirm the 90-day grace + 40% (1yr) / 25% (2yr) split, I’ll create a short commercial term-sheet and FedEx a mark to your legal team.

Available slots Thurs 9:30–10:30am PT for a 30-min call.

Marissa / Michael —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Orchard finance reviewed and returned a counter on two items:

1) Clawback cap: we can accept a 40% cap on a single-year contract only if the repayment excludes any credits tied to marketplace/promotional uplift (i.e., clawback applies to the springboard only). For a 2-year commitment we can accept a 30% cap but want no more than a 6-month repayment window.

2) True-up cadence & carryover: quarterly true-up is acceptable, but we need monthly reporting exports and the ability to request one out-of-cycle true-up per year without penalty. Also, any carryover into Q2 should not exceed 120% of Q1 forecast and should be explicitly limited to usage credits only (no discounts or promotional add-ons).

If those two points are acceptable, we're happy to move forward to a short commercial term-sheet and share it with our procurement.

I attached a short note from our finance team explaining their position.

Thanks,
Claire

Claire —

Thanks for the clear counter. We can sign up to the principles with two small commercial compromises that preserve both sides:

1) Clawback cap and exclusions: we accept a 40% cap on a 1yr deal (springboard only) and 30% on a 2yr deal. Redwood will exclude marketplace/promotional uplift from clawbacks as requested. Clawback repayment window: 6 months for 2yr, 9 months for 1yr (provides some runway but accelerates resolution).

2) True-up cadence & reporting: we will provide monthly exportable usage reports and permit one out-of-cycle true-up request per year (reasonable cause required). Carryover into Q2 limited to 120% of Q1 forecast and only for raw usage credits.

We’ll include language that any replenishment of the wallet to exceed forecast is auto-billed against committed spend and that replenished credits are subject to the same carryover rules. Marissa will put a short commercial term-sheet together and route a mark to your procurement/legal.
